questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: One of the most important aspects was that it had to be a city that I could see myself live in for a longer amount of time. I focused on a city with a lot of culture, nature close by and nice weather - Lisbon gave me all of that. Another aspect was the university. I wanted to study at a university which offered courses that I was interested in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: You get a lot of emails with all the informations needed, and if you are in doubt the International Relations Coordinator of Católica is there to help you.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Didn't really need any assistance since all the information you needed was in the emails you got before arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, however if you want to live in something else than a shared flat with a lot of other roommates, then it is pretty expensive. I shared a flat with the other exchange student from UCPH and that was very nice, however very expensive. I would recommend staying in a shared flat with other roommates, if you want to socialize with other students than the ones from your host university in an easy way.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is not possible to stay on campus so everybody lives off campus. Lisbon is such a nice city and Católica is pretty close with the metro.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was fine, however the courses got published very late.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You got an email with all the courses offered, and then you just checked of which ones you would like to attend. It was also possible to change later on, even after you already attended some of the classes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The International Relations Coordinator, Maria Ines, was very helpful if you had any questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted - so very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The courses end at different dates, and some at a late date. So if it is a priority for you to end your studies early then you should look for courses that offers that. However, you can always change your courses later on.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As a master student it is possible to choose to attend undergraduate courses or the LLM programme. I chose undergraduate courses and even though I had some of the courses before at UCPH I still learned something new and it was nice to have so background knowledge as it was also challenging for me to be taught in English.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As a student from UCPH then I think we will find the level at most other universities as lower compared to what we are used to. For me the most challenging was to be taught in English and learn all the legal terms in English. Therefore it was actually pretty nice with not such a high academic level, but I was also a master student attending undergraduate courses, so I think it was easier for me, then what undergraduate students will find it.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was pretty much the same - mostly the professors just teaching and a bit of group discussions. However the exams was very different. There were a lot of essays or questions where you had to give your opinion on a topic.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
EU Governance 
Introduction to EU Internal Market 
The Regulation of Technology Innovation 
EU Energy and Environmental Law 
Federalism and the EU 
Property 
Introduction to EU Competition Law
International Law of the Sea

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely Property. The professor was so good and really got you interested in the course. It regards US law, so it is also an opportunity to learn about another law system.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't encounter any unexpected costs. I spend a lot of money on food and personal spendings, because I traveled a lot and just really wanted to have all the experiences. You can definitely live in Lisbon for a lot less.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was way more expensive than what I expected, the housing market in Lisbon has really gone wild in the last few years. I also chose a more expensive option, you can definitely live for a lot less. Also it is not that cheap to buy groceries, but on the bright side it is pretty cheap (compared to Copenhagen) to eat out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were some, but not a lot.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some sport teams.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't attend any.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Portugal is really easy and cheap to travel around. I can recommend going to Ericeira for a surf camp (but there is also a lot of options to surf at a one of the many beaches in Lisbon), go watch the huge waves in Nazaré, take a trip to Porto and then you should definitely go to Madeira or the Azores. Lisbon itself is also such a nice city with so much to do. I spend a lot of weekends at the beaches, just chilled in the city or went to Cascais or Sintra.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I unfortunately only socialized with other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Everything goes so slow. Nobody is in a hurry.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated the slow living.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Everything goes really slow, you might as well just adjust to it as soon as possible. Hereby meaning also all the administrative things, that we are used to going fast at UCPH. 
All courses have mandatory attendance. 
It is hard to get the highest grades, but almost nobody fails any of the courses.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would attend the welcome sessions since it gives you a great opportunity to meet the other students quickly.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many students from other countries. My English has really improved and it is so nice to have friends in so many countries.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing. We looked way too late and therefore also ended up with speeding way too much. I would therefore recommend looking as early as possible. We thought it would be possible to see some of the flats, but that was not an option in any of the ones we looked at, so you might as well just book from home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
